note: Hand-authored fixture. First discovery call, earlier in the same deal as objection-call.

speakerNames.label: Prospect
speakerNames.name: Marcus
speakerNames.quote: Marcus? Hi. Sorry, I think I was two minutes late there.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Marcus? Hi. Sorry, I think I was two minutes late there.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: No, you're fine, I was still on the last one.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Ha. Yeah. Okay so — I've got half an hour, is that still right?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Half an hour, yeah.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Great. So before I show you anything, just tell me what's going on. What made you take the call?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Erm. So. We've got fourteen reps, and every one of them writes up calls differently. And half of them don't write them up at all, if I'm honest.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Which is fine until it isn't.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: What happens when it isn't?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Deals stall and nobody knows why. Like, I'll ask about something in the forecast and I get three different stories depending on who I ask.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: So the forecast is basically memory.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: It's built on vibes. Yeah.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Are you recording calls at the moment?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: We've got Chorus, so yeah, it records everything. That bit works fine.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: And the bit that doesn't?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Nobody trusts the summaries. Somebody read one that said a customer was ready to sign and — they'd said the opposite. On the actual call.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, that's the thing that kills it, isn't it. Once it's wrong in a way you can see.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Then you stop reading it. That's exactly what happened, usage fell off a cliff.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, so — the difference with what we do, and I'll show you, is every line points back at the moment. You click it, you land on the sentence.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Hang on, so I could actually check it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: You can check all of it. That's sort of the whole point.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Hm. Okay. That would change the conversation with my team, because the trust thing is the blocker. It's not the features.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Who else would need to be comfortable with it?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Dave in finance owns the budget. And security will want a look, because it's call recordings.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Sure. Is security a blocker or a checkpoint?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Checkpoint. They're reasonable if you fill the questionnaire in properly.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Okay. What would you want to see before you brought either of them in?

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Honestly? Run it on a real call of ours. Not a demo call. One of mine, with all the mess in it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I can do that. Send me a recording, I'll send you back the notes.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Alright. I'll pull one from last week, there's a good one where the customer just talks in circles for forty minutes.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Those are the good ones, genuinely.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Give me till Thursday though. I need to check I'm actually allowed to share it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No, of course. Thursday's fine, I'll turn it round same day.

segments.speaker: Prospect
segments.text: Right. Let's see if it holds up.
